stem: Ritu blows through a straw into a glass of clear lime water in her kitchen at home. After some time, the lime water turns milky. Why is this milky appearance evidence that carbon dioxide is present and a chemical change has taken place?

options.text: The milkiness is a new insoluble substance, calcium carbonate, formed when carbon dioxide reacts with calcium hydroxide
The milkiness appears because carbon dioxide dissolves in the water and makes it cloudy
The milkiness shows that the water has evaporated when warm air is blown into it
The milkiness is calcium hydroxide settling down at the bottom of the glass

teacher.key_rationale: Lime water is a solution of calcium hydroxide. Carbon dioxide reacts with it to form insoluble calcium carbonate, which appears milky; a new substance means a chemical change. B treats the milkiness as mere dissolving (no new substance), C wrongly invokes evaporation, and D wrongly suggests settling of the original solute.
